E1:
(1) Vending machine: a ProximityPrompt only shows when its parent gives it a world position: a BasePart, an Attachment, or a Model that has a PrimaryPart. Here its parent is a Folder, and the Folder sits in a Model with no PrimaryPart, so the prompt has no position and never shows. Fix: parent the prompt to a part, or better to an Attachment inside the machine's front part (e.g. Machine.Front.PromptAttachment). Setting VendingMachine.PrimaryPart and parenting the prompt to the Model also works.
(2) Lever: RequiresLineOfSight defaults to true. The prompt raycasts from the camera to the lever, and the glass case blocks that ray, so the prompt is hidden. Fix: set prompt.RequiresLineOfSight = false. Another option is to move the prompt to an Attachment or part outside the glass. You can also make the glass non-queryable (CanCollide = false and CanQuery = false), but then players can walk through it, so turning off line of sight is the usual fix.
E2:
- AlwaysOnTop = false: the tag is depth-tested, so walls hide it. With true, it always renders over 3D geometry.
- MaxDistance = 100: the tag is not drawn when the camera is more than 100 studs from the adornee. The default is infinite (0/inf), which is why it shows across the whole map.
- Size in Scale (studs) instead of Offset (pixels), e.g. Size = UDim2.fromScale(4, 1). The scale components of a BillboardGui's Size are world studs, so the tag shrinks with distance like a real object. Offset is fixed screen pixels, which is why it never changes size. Use TextScaled (with a UITextSizeConstraint if needed) on the label so the text follows the frame.
- Optional: StudsOffset / StudsOffsetWorldSpace = Vector3.new(0, 2, 0) to lift it above the head. Set LightInfluence = 0 to keep it readable at night.
- Optional: DistanceLowerLimit / DistanceUpperLimit / DistanceStep only matter for offset-sized gui scaling. Scale sizing is the simple fix.
E3:
With CharacterAutoLoads = false the engine never spawns characters, neither on join nor after death. Your scripts own spawning completely. RespawnTime is only used by the automatic respawn, so it does nothing now. Minimal server fix: call LoadCharacterAsync yourself (LoadCharacter was renamed in Jan 2026; the old name still works).
```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
Players.CharacterAutoLoads = false
local RESPAWN = 3
local function spawn(p) if p.Parent then p:LoadCharacterAsync() end end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(function(p)
  p.CharacterAdded:Connect(function(char)
    char:WaitForChild("Humanoid").Died:Connect(function()
      task.wait(RESPAWN); spawn(p)
    end)
  end)
  spawn(p) -- or wait for the round to start
end)
```
Connect CharacterAdded before the first spawn. Only spawn from the server. In a round game, gate spawn() on the round state (e.g. put dead players in a spectator queue).
E4:
CanQuery = false removes a part from all spatial queries: raycasts, shapecasts and GetPartsInPart / GetPartBoundsInBox. The RaycastParams filter can't bring it back. (CanQuery is only honoured when CanCollide is false, which is the case here.) So the laser can't see the glass.
Fix: set CanQuery = true on the glass and keep CanCollide = false. Players still walk through it, and raycasts hit it again (RespectCanCollide defaults to false, so non-colliding parts are still hit). If other rays (guns, camera) should ignore the glass, filter it per query instead: put the glass in a "Glass" collision group, or add it to those rays' ExcludeInstances / FilterDescendantsInstances. The laser's params leave it in.
E5:
Error 1: Instance:Clone() returns nil when the instance's Archivable is false. That is how the plugin's setting caused it: template:Clone() returned nil, then nil:PivotTo errors. Fix: set template.Archivable = true (and check descendants, since non-Archivable children are silently skipped in a clone). Add a guard: local g = template:Clone(); assert(g, "template not archivable").
Error 2: Destroy() sets Parent to nil and locks the Parent property permanently. It also disconnects connections and marks the instance for cleanup, so a destroyed instance can never be reparented. Destroy is final; never reuse a destroyed template.
Correct pattern: keep one Archivable template in ReplicatedStorage or ServerStorage and never parent or destroy it. For each spawn, Clone, then PivotTo, then set Parent = workspace. When the goblin dies, Destroy the clone (e.g. Debris or a Humanoid.Died handler). To reuse instances (pooling), set Parent = nil (or move to a storage folder) instead of Destroy, then reset health and state before respawning.

```lua
local Players = game:GetService("Players")
local SIZE = Vector3.new(6, 5, 6)
local function swing(attacker: Model)
  local root = attacker:FindFirstChild("HumanoidRootPart")
  if not root then return end
  local params = OverlapParams.new()
  params.FilterType = Enum.RaycastFilterType.Exclude
  params.FilterDescendantsInstances = {attacker} -- 2026: params.ExcludeInstances = {attacker}
  local cf = root.CFrame * CFrame.new(0, 0, -3) -- 3 studs in front
  local hit = {}
  for _, part in workspace:GetPartBoundsInBox(cf, SIZE, params) do
    local model = part:FindFirstAncestorOfClass("Model")
    local hum = model and model:FindFirstChildOfClass("Humanoid")
    if hum and not hit[hum] and hum.Health > 0 then
      hit[hum] = true -- once per swing
      hum:TakeDamage(20)
    end
  end
end
```

Caveat: GetPartBoundsInBox tests the parts' axis-aligned bounding boxes, not their real shapes. Rotated or odd-shaped parts can register a hit slightly outside the box. For exact geometry use GetPartsInPart with a box part (more expensive). Run it on the server with a swing cooldown, and check the attacker's distance and state there. Don't trust client hit claims.

E11:
Use MemoryStoreService for both (fast, short-lived, cross-server). DataStores are too slow and have write limits.
- Matchmaking queue: MemoryStoreQueue (GetQueue(name, invisibilityTimeout), default 30 s). AddAsync(value, expiration, priority) gives priority then FIFO. Servers ReadAsync(2, ...) to pull a pair, teleport them (TeleportService:ReserveServer), then RemoveAsync(id). Items read are invisible until removed and reappear if the server crashes. Optionally keep a HashMap or SortedMap for per-player status and cancel.
- Hourly top 100: MemoryStoreSortedMap. One map per hour bucket, e.g. "Scores_" .. os.time()//3600, with an expiration of about 1-2 h. Use UpdateAsync(userId, keep max, expiration) and a numeric sort key. GetRangeAsync(Descending, 100) returns at most 200 per call.
Limits that shape the design:
- Expiration is required, max 45 days.
- Value up to 32 KB. Keys and string sort keys up to 128 characters.
- A sorted map holds up to 1M items / 100 MB.
- Memory quota is 64 KB + 1.2 KB × total users, experience-wide.
- Requests are 1,000 + 120 × CCU units/min experience-wide. GetRangeAsync costs the items returned, and ReadAsync waits cost extra. Each queue or map is one partition (~30k units/min).
Cache the top 100 per server and refresh it every 30-60 s instead of every client and frame. Handle TotalRequestsOverLimit / TotalMemoryOverLimit with pcall and backoff.
E12:
Your design uses 40 reads + 40 writes per minute per server for autosave (UpdateAsync counts as a read and a write), plus bursts when players leave.
- Per-server defaults (standard DataStore): read/write/remove 60 + players × 40 per minute, which is 1,660 at 40 players. List is 5 + players × 2. Ordered writes are 30 + players × 5.
- Experience-wide budgets since 2026-07-29, shared by all servers and Open Cloud, are now the binding limit. Read 300 + CCU × 40, Write 300 + CCU × 20, List 300 + CCU × 2, Remove 300 + CCU × 40 per minute. Check them with DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType before bulk work.
- Per key: value up to 4,194,304 characters (4 MB serialized). Key name up to 50 characters ("Player_<UserId>" fits). Write throughput 4 MB/min per key and reads 25 MB/min per key, each request rounded up to the next KB. Rapid repeated writes to one key get throttled/queued, so don't save the same key back-to-back (leave/autosave overlap): debounce per player.
- Storage: 500 MB + 1 MB × lifetime players.
Also: stagger autosaves, don't yield inside the UpdateAsync transform, pcall with backoff, save all players in BindToClose within the ~30 s window, and use session locking to prevent cross-server overwrites.
E13:
Flow (all on the server):
1. The client sends the raw name through a RemoteEvent. The server validates its type and length and rate-limits the remote.
2. Server: local ok, result = pcall(TextService.FilterStringAsync, TextService, name, player.UserId, Enum.TextFilterContext.PublicChat).
3. Since everyone sees it, display result:GetNonChatStringForBroadcastAsync() (not ...ForUserAsync, which is for one recipient). Put that filtered string in the replicated label or attribute.
4. If filtering errors, don't show the raw text: show nothing or a default name, and retry later.
5. Persistence: save the original raw name (or the filtered one) in the DataStore. On every load, filter it again before displaying, because filter rules and the owner's account settings change and the filter result object can't be stored. Never show stored text unfiltered.
Never filter on the client. Never trust a client-supplied 'already filtered' string.
E14:
Architecture: Discord bot, then Open Cloud Messaging API, then MessagingService in every live server, then clients.
1. External call: the bot does an HTTPS POST to Open Cloud, POST https://apis.roblox.com/cloud/v2/universes/{universeId}:publishMessage, with body {"topic": "Announcements", "message": "<text>"}. (The legacy v1 is /messaging-service/v1/universes/{id}/topics/{topic}.)
2. Credentials: an Open Cloud API key created in the Creator Hub by the experience owner (or group), with the universe-messaging-service:publish permission scoped to this experience. Send it in the x-api-key header. Restrict allowed IPs, store it as a secret on the bot server, never in game code, and rotate it if leaked.
3. In-game: a server Script runs pcall(MessagingService.SubscribeAsync, MessagingService, "Announcements", function(msg) ... end) at startup. msg.Data is the text and msg.Sent is the timestamp. It then FireAllClients on a RemoteEvent, and a LocalScript shows the banner. Filter or validate the text if users can author it.
Limits: message 1 KB (1,024 characters). Best-effort delivery, usually under a second. Shares the experience's messaging limits (e.g. receives per topic 40 + 80 × servers per minute; subscriptions per server 20 + 8 × players). For must-arrive state, also store it in a DataStore or config and treat the message as a nudge to reload.
E15:
Half-built building: with StreamingEnabled, parts of a Model stream in separately, and a LocalScript may run before they all arrive. Fixes:
- Set the building Model's ModelStreamingMode = Atomic. The whole model arrives (and leaves) as one unit once it is in range. The client still waits for the model itself with WaitForChild, or uses CollectionService tags plus GetInstanceAddedSignal instead of assuming it exists. Never assume it exists at script start.
- The server can call Player:RequestStreamAroundAsync(position, timeout) before teleporting a player near it. Use pcall and a bounded timeout. It is a request, not a guarantee.
Scoreboard always present: set ModelStreamingMode = Persistent. It is sent after join, before workspace.PersistentLoaded fires, and never streamed out. PersistentPerPlayer plus Model:AddPersistentPlayer(player) makes it persistent only for chosen players. Or keep pure-data parts out of Workspace (ReplicatedStorage is always fully replicated, but doesn't render).
Trade-offs:
- Atomic: one big model streams in late and all at once, and stays loaded until every part is out of range (more memory).
- Persistent: always uses memory and bandwidth on every client and slows join, so use it sparingly for small models.
- Streamed-out instances are parented to nil (not destroyed), so handle removal too.
- Tune StreamingMinRadius / TargetRadius (e.g. 64 / 1024).
E16:
Aim direction: yes, switch it to UnreliableRemoteEvent. It is a high-frequency stream where only the latest value matters. A dropped or late packet is replaced 33 ms later, and reliable ordering would only add latency (head-of-line blocking) under packet loss.
Hit reports: no, keep them on a reliable RemoteEvent. They are discrete state-changing events that must arrive exactly once, and a lost hit is a visible bug. The server still validates each hit (fire rate, line of sight, distance, timestamp) and never trusts client damage.
Limits:
- UnreliableRemoteEvent payload max is about 1,000 bytes; larger payloads are dropped silently. Pack data tightly (e.g. a buffer or a compressed direction).
- Delivery is unordered and not guaranteed. Messages with no connected handler are discarded, not queued. Under load, excess unreliable traffic is dropped rather than delayed.
- RemoteEvents are ordered and reliable. When throttled (roughly 500 requests/s per client shared across remotes) they are delayed, not dropped.
- Rate-limit and validate arguments on the server for both. Also consider sending aim at 20 Hz with interpolation.
E17:
```lua
-- 2 + 4*3 = 14 bytes
local function pack(id: number, pos: Vector3): buffer
  local b = buffer.create(14)
  buffer.writeu16(b, 0, math.clamp(id, 0, 65535))
  buffer.writef32(b, 2, pos.X)
  buffer.writef32(b, 6, pos.Y)
  buffer.writef32(b, 10, pos.Z)
  return b
end
local function unpack(b: buffer): (number, Vector3)
  if typeof(b) ~= "buffer" or buffer.len(b) ~= 14 then return nil end -- validate on server
  return buffer.readu16(b, 0), Vector3.new(
    buffer.readf32(b, 2), buffer.readf32(b, 6), buffer.readf32(b, 10))
end
-- sender:  ProjectileUpdate:FireAllClients(pack(id, part.Position))
-- receiver: ProjectileUpdate.OnClientEvent:Connect(function(b) local id, pos = unpack(b) end)
```
Buffer rules:
- Offsets are zero-based byte offsets.
- Fixed size from buffer.create(size). It never grows, and out-of-range reads or writes throw. The bytes start zeroed.
- Little-endian. Integer writes truncate or wrap, so clamp first.
- f32 keeps about 7 significant digits, so don't compare round-tripped floats with ==.
- Buffers replicate through remotes as compact binary, and 14 bytes is well under the ~1,000-byte unreliable limit.
- On the server, check NaN/inf (math.isfinite) on received positions.
E18:
Every unanchored assembly (the welded cart is one assembly) is physically simulated by one network owner: the server or a client. By default the engine assigns it automatically, usually to the nearest player, and can switch owners as players move. Each handover causes a hitch, and if the server or another player owns the cart, the driver's inputs go through a round trip, which shows up as stutter and lag.
Server fix: when the VehicleSeat.Occupant changes to a player's humanoid, call seat.AssemblyRootPart:SetNetworkOwner(player) (or any part in the assembly). When the seat empties, call SetNetworkOwner(nil) to give it to the server, or SetNetworkOwnershipAuto(). Only works on unanchored parts on the server (errors for anchored ones). Check CanSetNetworkOwnership() first.
Kill brick: while the client owns the cart, the client simulates its physics and the server only gets replicated positions. Touched on the server fires from the client-reported (possibly lagged, interpolated or exploit-modified) movement, so touches can arrive late, at odd positions, multiple times, or be faked. Make the kill brick act only on character parts: resolve Players:GetPlayerFromCharacter(hit.Parent), ignore cart parts, debounce, and sanity-check the position. Never rely on client-owned physics for authoritative logic.

Changes (Roblox docs, as of 2026):
- Request/access limits: since 2026-07-29 there are experience-wide budgets shared by all servers and Open Cloud, with a base of 300 (was 250). Per minute: Read 300 + CCU × 40, Write 300 + CCU × 20, List 300 + CCU × 2, Remove 300 + CCU × 40. The old per-server limits (60 + players × 40 etc.) still exist but are no longer the binding limit.
- Storage: 500 MB + 1 MB × lifetime players (was a 100 MB base). Only the latest version of each key counts, measured compressed.
What to do:
- Use DataStoreService:GetRequestBudgetForRequestType to throttle migrations, admin tools and Open Cloud jobs, leaving headroom for live saves. An external script can now starve live servers.
- Don't retry throttled calls in tight loops: back off.
- Don't pre-compress data (Roblox compresses for you). Store binary as base64 strings, since strings must be valid UTF-8.
- Keep saves lean, batch writes, debounce per-key saves, and clean up or remove dead keys to stay under storage.
- Errors 301-306 mean the request queue is full, so saves may take 10-30 s before failing. Plan for it in BindToClose.
E20:
New properties on both RaycastParams and OverlapParams: IncludeInstances and ExcludeInstances (alongside CollisionGroup, RespectCanCollide, BruteForceAllSlow).
Behavior vs the old pair:
- The old FilterDescendantsInstances + FilterType (Include/Exclude) gave one list in one mode. You couldn't include a subtree and also exclude something inside it.
- The new properties are independent and combine. IncludeInstances: nil = everything, {} = nothing. ExcludeInstances removes instances and their descendants. When an instance is in both, exclusion wins.
- The old properties still work but are documented as superseded.
```lua
local params = RaycastParams.new()
params.IncludeInstances = {workspace.Map}
params.ExcludeInstances = {workspace.Map.Glass}
local result = workspace:Raycast(origin, direction, params)
```
Gotchas:
- Build params once and update the arrays when the world changes, not per ray.
- Parts with CanQuery = false (and CanCollide = false) are never hit regardless of the filters.

MarketplaceService:BindReceiptHandler(receiptType: Enum.ReceiptType, handler, filter?) returns an RBXScriptConnection.
- Receipt types: DeveloperProduct, RobuxTransferSender, RobuxTransferReceiver.
- The handler receives the receipt info (PurchaseId, PlayerId, ProductId, ...). It must return Enum.ReceiptDecision.Processed only after the grant and the PurchaseId record are durably saved. Otherwise it returns NotProcessedYet, or errors, and Roblox redelivers the receipt later.

```lua
  local ok = grantAndRecord(info.PlayerId, info.PurchaseId, MY_PRODUCTS[info.ProductId]) -- idempotent save
```

E24:
Luau's math library added built-ins that replace common hand-rolled helpers:
- math.lerp(a: number, b: number, t: number): number. Returns a + (b - a) * t. A t outside 0..1 extrapolates.
- math.map(x: number, inMin: number, inMax: number, outMin: number, outMax: number): number. Linear remap from [inMin, inMax] to [outMin, outMax]. It does not clamp, so wrap it in math.clamp if needed.
- math.isnan(x), math.isinf(x), math.isfinite(x) each return a boolean. Use them to validate remote numbers instead of x ~= x tricks.
- Constants such as math.tau and math.e, plus existing helpers like math.clamp, math.sign, math.round and math.noise.
Check that your Studio version has them. Prefer these built-ins over custom lerp/remap functions, since they are faster and clearer.
